title: Ops instrumentation corral and quickflows
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Build an "corral" service that provides a lightweight runtime and telemetry fabric for admin utilities and runbooks-as-tasks, plus a 'quickflows' layer for common short remediation flows. The corral should: 1) provide a simple API to register, invoke, and version small admin flows (idempotent tasks with typed inputs); 2) emit rich usage telemetry (who invoked, params scrubbed, duration, outcome) to the Ops telemetry pipeline; 3) enforce RBAC and canary rollout flags; 4) support dry-run and replay modes for testing; 5) ship with a library of 10-15 quickflows (restart service, rotate key, scale pool) as reference implementations.

Why: current runbooks are scattered (GDocs + ad-hoc scripts). Oncall spends time copying playbook steps and we lack consistent instrumentation for post-incident analysis. The corral is intended to reduce mean-time-to-remediate for common fixes and enable us to link remediation actions to telemetry for SLOs/automation insights.

Non-goals: full workflow engine or replacing large multi-step orchestration platforms. Corral is intentionally minimal (synchronous calls + small idempotent tasklets) to keep latency low.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Public API and SDK for invoking quickflows (REST + internal JS/Go SDK).
- Telemetry events available in the Ops analytics dashboard (traceable to request/token and runbook id) with PII scrubbed.
- RBAC enforced via existing SSO groups and auditable audit-log entry for every execution.
- 10 curated quickflows delivered, each with unit tests and e2e dry-run capability.
- Canary rollout in internal dev org (20% of oncall traffic) with automatic rollback on failure rate > 2%.

Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood/ops/corral-design-836995, initial PR: https://github.com/redwood/ops-corral/pull/142, telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/ops-corral/quickflows-usage
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Khan: Created ticket and high-level design. Initial list of quickflows attached in Confluence. Tracked as part of Internal Ops Modernization.

2026-03-11 Marco Ruiz: Spike completed — prototyped local corral process with HTTP API and a simple JS SDK. Observed ~8ms median overhead for trivial tasks. Prototype repo: github.com/redwood/ops-corral (branch prototyped-api).

2026-03-12 Priya Shah (SRE): Telemetry plan review: prefer event-batching to avoid explosion of small Kafka messages; sampling policy for low-risk runs. Concern: need stronger param-scrubbing rules for 'rotate-key' flow. Open: agree on scrub regex and KMS integration approach.

2026-03-13 Design review: Added quickflow UX in Console — ‘Runbook shortcuts’ panel to surface approved quickflows with explanations and 'dry run' toggle. Design notes at https://drive.redwood/designs/ops-quickflows-v1.
2026-03-14 Marco Ruiz: Implemented RBAC adapter using existing SSO group service. Demo PR created: https://github.com/redwood/ops-corral/pull/142. Needs security review for audit log format.

2026-03-15 Security (Ethan Clarke): Quick scan done. Need to ensure secrets never land in plain text telemetry; suggest client-side redaction and server-side validators. Marking security_review_required=true. Action: schedule ad-hoc review with KMS/crypto team next week.
2026-03-15 Marco Ruiz: Updated API to include dry-run flag and added a replay token header. Draft e2e tests added in github.com/redwood/ops-corral/tree/integration-tests.

Action items:
- Marco: finish telemetry batching + redactors (ETA 2026-03-22).
- Priya: finalize scrub rules and run the first security-focused dry-run (ETA 2026-03-20).
- Aisha: coordinate canary rollout plan with oncall schedule and prepare rollback playbook (ETA 2026-03-25).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: event-batching reduces write-amplification but increases latency for near-real-time dashboards. Decided to batch with a 3s flush window and a max batch size of 200 events. Using JSON proto v2 for compatibility; evaluated protobuf but deferred for speed of iteration.

2. Implement corral service core and internal SDKs (JS/Go).
3. Add RBAC/audit integration and dry-run mode.
4. Ship first 10 quickflows and unit/e2e tests.
5. Canary rollout + monitoring and rollback automation.
